problems.title: The released CDA objective is a different tensor operation
problems.source_location: Eqs.(1)–(4), pp.4–5; src/loss/CDA_loss.py, lines 11–48; src/model/MultiModel_PL.py, lines 199–203
claim: Temporal covariance should be \(HH^{\top}/(T-1)\). The code permutes \((B,d,C,T)\) to \((B,d,T,C)\), reshapes back without undoing the interleaving, zeros the diagonal and uses unsquared Frobenius distance.
analysis: For centered \(H=[(-1,0,1);(-2,0,2)]\), correct covariance is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The permute/reshape instead forms rows \((-1,-2,0),(0,1,2)\), yielding \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}5/2&-1\\-1&5/2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), then returns diagonal-zero matrix with cross-entry \(-1\), not \(2\), and eigenvalues \(1,-1\). Even otherwise correct diagonal deletion makes \(I_2\) and \(4I_2\) identical despite squared distance \(18\). Separately, a valid covariance difference \(D=[(0,2);(2,0)]\) contributes \(\log(1+\sqrt8)\), not the paper’s \(\log9\). No constant coefficient adjustment equates the two powers generally.
result: The current path does not implement the written covariance/centroid objective. It could define another regularizer, but the interleaving is not a covariance convention; experimental effects remain unknown.
repair: Retain centered channel/time ordering, compute \(HH^{\top}/(T-1)\) for \(T>1\), preserve diagonals and sum squared centroid differences. The matrix identity proves correspondence; new pretraining and ablations would assess effects.

problems.impact_rationale: The exact release realization differs from the paper, without an identified historical pretraining rerun or reversal of core empirical results.

problems.title: Checkpoint choice uses final evaluation subjects
claim: The subjects labeled test determine maximum validation-accuracy checkpoint selection and are reused for final predictions.
analysis: The same loader enters training validation, best-model selection and final scoring. Exclusion from gradient updates does not remove this dependency. For four independent fair test labels and fixed constant-zero/constant-one candidates, selecting the better test accuracy has expectation \(11/16\), while each fixed candidate has expectation \(1/2\). This is a selection illustration, not estimated inflation here. A separate unpublished final-test implementation could change historical attribution.
result: The released score is test-dependent selection accuracy rather than untouched-subject performance. No claim that every published table used this script is made.
repair: Use subject-level development data for selection and untouched outer test subjects for final reporting, or fix an epoch before seeing those outcomes.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The source dependency is clear but remains a release-level evaluation issue with historical outcome magnitude unresolved.

problems.title: DEAP labels require an unavailable ordering contract
problems.source_location: Section 3.1 and Appendix E.8; src/data/io_utils.py, lines 421–465; train_mlp_full.py, lines 68–71
claim: The paper defines participant-rating median splits, but the loader returns \(20\) zeros then \(20\) ones for every subject and evaluation tiles one label vector.
analysis: Two subjects with first/last half ratings \((1,9)\) and \((9,1)\) both have median \(5\), yet complementary correct labels. A single tiled vector cannot match both; this is a valid protocol witness, not actual DEAP data. The code may depend on per-subject label-sorted preprocessing or shared stimulus labels, but the required original trial permutations and affective dimension are unavailable. Subject-specific sorting must also preserve correct stimulus pairing.
result: The released route alone does not specify the rating-based task. Without actual preprocessing/labels, wrong published DEAP accuracy is not established.
repair: Recover subject/trial/dimension-indexed labels and any permutations, with explicit median/tie rules and stimulus-aligned pairing. No numerical correction is established.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The discrepancy is conditional on an unresolved upstream identity/order convention.
